name: UK

flag.title: The Union Jack
flag.note: Red, white & blue cross of three nations

lead: The UK is four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Shakespeare, the steam engine, the Web and football all came from here. Once it ruled a quarter of the Earth.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The UK covers Great Britain and the north of Ireland. The English Channel, just 34 km wide at its narrowest, separates it from Europe. Scotland's Highlands have lochs (lakes) and craggy mountains.
The coastline stretches over 17,800 km. No point in England is more than 113 km from the sea.
animals: The red squirrel is Britain's native squirrel. It is now rare because the larger grey squirrel arrived from America in 1876. Puffins nest on rocky sea cliffs each spring.
The robin is Britain's unofficial national bird. It is bold enough to perch on a gardener's spade.
culture: The British love a queue, an orderly waiting line. People brew tea over 100 million times every day.
The BBC, a TV and radio company, began in 1927 and is the world's oldest national broadcaster. Bonfire Night on 5 November fills the sky with fireworks.
history: Romans invaded in 43 AD. The Normans, soldiers from France, arrived in 1066, the last successful invasion. Magna Carta, a paper limiting the king's power, planted the seed of modern democracy in 1215.
The Industrial Revolution began here in the 1760s and turned the world from farms to factories. In 1948 Britain created the NHS, a free health service.
wows: London's Underground opened in 1863 as the world's first metro (underground railway).
Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist, invented the World Wide Web and gave it away free.
Britain has no single written rule book for government, only centuries-old laws and customs.
The UK enters four football teams in World Cup qualifying: England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire in Mexico began.
Only the US has had more winners of the Nobel Prize, a top world award, than the UK.
Big Ben is only the bell, and the tower is the Elizabeth Tower.

myths.myth: It rains every single day in Britain
myths.fact: London gets less rain each year than Rome or Miami. It drizzles often, but rarely pours.
Parliament and the Prime Minister make the real decisions. The King's job is mostly ceremonial (for show).
